# create_timer — Example systemd units

These are the actual unit files generated by `install_timer.sh`. The
file paths and content are examples; real values depend on the
`--schedule`, `--prompt`, and `--name` arguments passed.

## Example install

```bash
pie/<agent_name>/skills/create_timer/scripts/install_timer.sh \
  the sibling-invoice \
  --schedule "*-*-7 09:00:00 Australia/Brisbane" \
  --prompt "Generate this week's the sibling invoice using the
            book-keeper skill, then email it to customer@example.com"
```

## Generated files

### `pie/<agent>/systemd/the sibling-invoice.service`

```ini
# Generated by create_timer/install_timer.sh on 2026-10-15T12:30:00+10:00
# Target: harness /api/v1/internal/timer (the harness)
# Agent: <agent_name>
# Schedule: *-*-7 09:00:00 Australia/Brisbane
# Edit + commit to update; run install_timer.sh to reinstall.
[Unit]
Description=create_timer wake for <task-name> (agent=<agent_name>)
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
WorkingDirectory=<harness_root>
ExecStart=<harness_root>/skills/create_timer/scripts/wake_agent_main.sh ~/.config/systemd/user/<task-name>.prompt <agent_name>
EnvironmentFile=-<harness_root>/.env
```

### `pie/<agent>/systemd/the sibling-invoice.timer`

```ini
# Generated by create_timer/install_timer.sh on 2026-10-15T12:30:00+10:00
# Schedule: *-*-7 09:00:00 Australia/Brisbane
[Unit]
Description=create_timer schedule for the sibling-invoice
Requires=the sibling-invoice.service

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-7 09:00:00 Australia/Brisbane
Persistent=true
Unit=the sibling-invoice.service

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```

### `pie/<agent>/systemd/the sibling-invoice.prompt`

```
Generate this week's the sibling invoice using the book-keeper skill,
then email it to customer@example.com
```

## Runtime counterparts

The same three files are also copied to
`~/.config/systemd/user/<name>.{service,timer,prompt}`. The git-tracked
copies in `pie/<agent>/systemd/` are the source of truth; the runtime
copies are regenerated by `install_timer.sh`.

## systemd quirks to be aware of

- **Path**: systemd --user services start with a sanitized PATH
  (`/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin`).
  The wake script needs `curl`, `python3`, and `bash` — all in the
  default PATH. If your OS doesn't include `/usr/bin` in that list,
  add `PATH=...` to the .service's `[Service]` section.
- **EnvironmentFile**: the `-` prefix means "tolerate missing file".
  If the .env is deleted, the service still starts but
  `HARNESS_INTERNAL_TOKEN` is empty and the wake POST returns 401.
- **Linger**: the service user MUST have linger enabled for
  systemd --user timers to survive logout:
  ```bash
  sudo loginctl enable-linger <service_user>
  ```
- **Calendar timezone**: `OnCalendar=*-*-7 09:00:00` (no timezone)
  is interpreted in the system's local time. To be explicit, use
  `Australia/Brisbane` (or another IANA TZ).
- **Persistent=true**: missed runs (e.g., when the machine was off)
  fire as soon as the system is up again. Without this, a missed run
  is skipped.
